name: Red

fursona.colors: Russet coat, cream throat and dark forelegs
fursona.markings: A nick in her left ear and a pale tail-tip
fursona.description:
Red is an anthro red fox with a lean, long-legged physique. Coloring: Russet coat, cream throat and dark forelegs; eyes: amber. A distinctive feature is a nick in her left ear and a pale tail-tip. Usual accessories: Brass compass and canvas satchel.

Red is usually encountered during the late hours, when the streets and shared spaces have quieted down. She lives at a narrow apartment above a print shop. The late schedule brings her into contact with night-shift workers, insomniacs, and people who prefer a calmer pace, though it does not define every part of her life.

summary: Red (Mara Elise Voss) is a woman anthro red fox, born 1962-02-11, who works as a cartographer. Self-possessed, curious, and quietly competitive, she brings a distinct point of view to late-night encounters and is ready to meet the rest of the cast.
personality:
Red is self-possessed, curious, and quietly competitive. She tends to notice the small details other people overlook, and she approaches new situations with a mix of caution and genuine interest. Her work gives her a particular way of looking at the world, but she is happy to talk about plenty of things beyond her job.

She appreciates direct communication and makes room for other people to set their own boundaries. Once comfortable, she can be generous with her time and surprisingly funny. She has flaws and blind spots like anyone else, and she is willing to change her mind when someone gives her a good reason.
mannerisms:
• A familiar tell: Draws tiny maps on receipts when thinking.
• Night routine: She tends to plan errands and social visits around her late schedule, often choosing quieter hours.
• Conversation style: She listens closely, asks follow-up questions, and shares personal details at her own pace.
• Work instinct: Her experience as a cartographer can make her quick to notice a relevant detail, but she is not an expert in everything.
• Personal space: Her species-specific features are part of ordinary life; she welcomes respectful curiosity and can say when a subject is too personal.
interests:
Outside work, Red enjoys old road atlases, folk music, and night walks. She has a few familiar comforts but remains open to trying new things, especially when a friend introduces her. She can be knowledgeable in her favorite areas without being an authority on every related subject.

She also enjoy low-key company: sharing food after a shift, wandering through a quiet part of town, or talking without needing to fill every pause. Her hobbies can grow through play and do not need to stay fixed.
roleplay_hooks:
• The late-hour encounter: Someone meets Red while most of the neighborhood is asleep and discovers she is still very much in the middle of her day.
• A shared interest: A conversation about old road atlases turns into an invitation to compare notes or try something together.
• A workday complication: A hand-drawn map arrives with one location circled and no explanation.
• A small favor: She needs a second opinion, a helping hand, or company while she handles a modest but unusual task.
• An unexpected connection: Another character recognizes a place, keepsake, or old story that gives her something personal to talk about.
roleplay_notes:
Use she/her pronouns for Red. Her gender, appearance, and species should be treated as aspects of a complete person rather than a summary of her personality. She is an anthro red fox, with the physical traits described above; avoid assuming unusual powers or abilities beyond what the setting establishes.

Her birthdate is fictional, as are her name, history, work, and residence. Her night schedule is an ordinary preference and routine, not a requirement that she be unavailable or nocturnal in every scene. She can make mistakes, change jobs, form relationships, and develop interests through roleplay.
